bullets.title: META surges 30%+ in Sept on Muse AI agent launch; Goldman desk flags 'agentic anxiety' in financials
bullets.body: META gained roughly +32.7% this month, its strongest monthly performance since 2013, driven by the new Muse AI agent launch. Goldman's desk flagged 'agentic anxiety' spreading into bank stocks, with the GSXUSWCH consumer inertia basket falling 2.58% while big-tech bid. Hedgeye raised META to $1,200+ target and confirmed a bullish trend breakout signal.

bullets.title: SHOP +7.3% on Muse integration; META-Shopify partnership enables AI-driven checkout
bullets.body: Shopify rallied 7.3% after CEO Tobi Lutke confirmed a partnership with Meta's Muse to enable agentic checkout via Shop Pay across all Shopify stores. Amazon separately blocked Meta's Muse agents from accessing its retail platform, framing the move as competitive positioning against AI-driven commerce.

bullets.title: AMD hits $1T market cap for first time; INTC surges 13%+ as CPU demand narrative takes hold
bullets.body: AMD stock crossed $1 trillion market cap—its first ever—rallying ~10% on the session, as Intel jumped 12–14% on a narrative that agentic AI requires far more CPUs relative to GPUs (3–4x ratio for inference vs. 7–8x for training). Analysts noted TSMC advanced nodes are fully booked and Intel 18A is positioned as the pragmatic base die partner for SK Hynix and Micron.

bullets.title: NVDA forward P/E hits decade-low at 15.75; board member Mark Stevens sells $300M in shares
bullets.body: Nvidia's forward P/E fell to 15.75, the lowest in over 10 years, even as chip stocks broadly rallied. Separately, board member Mark Stevens—one of NVDA's largest shareholders—sold $300M in shares, flagged on fintwit as a potential insider signal worth monitoring.

bullets.title: Michael Burry increases shorts on MU, NBIS, and PLTR
bullets.body: Michael Burry disclosed increased short positions in Micron (MU), Nebius (NBIS), and Palantir (PLTR), making him a notable bear on the AI/semiconductor complex even as sector peers rallied. Burry's shorts were corroborated by multiple sources in the digest window.

bullets.title: MU and NVDA show strongest bullish options flow; MU target raised to $1,200
bullets.body: MU and NVDA were neck-and-neck for most bullish options flow on Monday, with a whale buying ~$15M in short-dated MU calls. Separately, a technical analyst raised MU's price target to $1,200 and flagged a bullish breakout. Hedgeye also confirmed a bullish trend breakout signal on MU.

bullets.title: AVGO and NVDA supply-constrained; memory LTAs run through 2031
bullets.body: A well-sourced thread noted Broadcom expects 100% supply-constrained YoY growth for the next two years, while NVDA expects 70% supply-constrained growth next year. Memory long-term agreements span until 2031, and a massive demand-supply imbalance in lasers is expected. Silicon wafer prices (12-inch epitaxial) are forecast to rise 15–25% in 2027 as capacity expansion drives demand.

bullets.title: NBIS implements up to 20% GPU price hikes; H200 and H100 pricing revised
bullets.body: Nebius raised H200 on-demand pricing 19.1% and H100 by 16.5%, with B300 at its highest on-demand price from any vendor. Prior price hike announcements drove NBIS stock $20+ higher. One analyst flagged NBIS's financing model as more sustainable than CRWV and other neocloud peers.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 18 Pro sees 60–70% YoY Taiwan sales surge; TSMC 2nm chips shipping
bullets.body: Taiwan telcos reported 70% YoY growth in iPhone 18 Pro sales in the first three days after launch. TSMC's 2nm chips are confirmed in production and shipping in the iPhone 18 Pro series and several flagship Android devices. Apple's market cap approached $5T as stock hit 52-week highs.

bullets.title: MSFT upgraded to Buy at Stifel with $575 PT; launches Copilot 'super app' with discounts
bullets.body: Stifel upgraded Microsoft to Buy and raised its price target to $575, citing sustainable mid-to-upper teens revenue growth from LLM advancement and Azure strength. Separately, Microsoft launched an AI 'super app' with boosted Copilot discounts to drive broader adoption.

bullets.title: AMZN trading at AWS + Anthropic stake value with zero assigned to rest; bull case on VM pricing
bullets.body: One analyst argued AMZN stock effectively prices in only AWS and its Anthropic stake with zero value assigned to other business segments, and sees AWS positioned to gain pricing leverage from VM infrastructure demand. AMZN was also flagged in Trump's July disclosure as a $5–25M sale.

bullets.title: Fed hikes 25bps; markets now price 50/50 odds of another hike; Fed hawkish rhetoric intensifies
bullets.body: The Fed delivered a 25bp rate hike last week, reversing early-2026 rate-cut expectations. Fed's Goolsbee warned restoring price stability 'won't be painless' and said supply shocks are proving persistent. Fed's Collins voted for the hike citing Middle East conflict risks to energy prices, and said more restrictive rates are needed.

bullets.title: Diesel hits all-time high $6.53/gal; Trump weighs export ban; BofA raises Brent to $95
bullets.body: U.S. diesel prices hit a record $6.53/gallon, up 76% YoY, with the Strait of Hormuz severely disrupted (only 2–3 vessels crossing vs. 125/day pre-conflict). Trump and top Republicans weighed a diesel export ban; BofA raised its H2 2026 Brent forecast to $95. Goldman warned the refining crisis could persist through 2027.

bullets.title: Taiwan export orders surge 71.4% YoY in August to record $103B, beating 63% consensus
bullets.body: Taiwan's August export orders reached $102.96B, up 71.4% YoY and well above the 63% consensus estimate. AI demand and custom ASIC chip design orders were cited as the drivers of the upside surprise, reinforcing the broader semiconductor demand narrative.

bullets.title: Market breadth deteriorating: 6th straight day of more 52-week lows than highs; SPX rally size-led
bullets.body: Multiple sources flagged deteriorating breadth—the S&P 500 equal-weight index gained only 18bps vs. ~150bps for cap-weighted SPX, the largest mega-cap/small-cap spread in 5+ years. Monday's close marked the sixth consecutive day of more 52-week lows than highs, with under 30% of S&P stocks above their 50-day moving average.

bullets.title: AWS wins first NATO RESTRICTED cloud approval across all 32 NATO nations
bullets.body: AWS became the first cloud provider approved for NATO RESTRICTED workloads across all 32 NATO member nations, a meaningful competitive moat in defense cloud and potential accelerant for government AI contracts.

bullets.title: COHR launches PhotonLink integrated optics platform for AI datacenters at ECOC 2026
bullets.body: Coherent officially launched PhotonLink at ECOC 2026, its integrated optics platform spanning the full optical signal chain from light generation through reception and supporting co-packaged optics (CPO). LITE and GLW were also highlighted demonstrating high-density optical die-to-die interconnect at the same event.

bullets.title: GEV accelerates $200B backlog target to early 2027; contracted turbine guidance appears conservative
bullets.body: GE Vernova now expects to reach $200B of backlog by early 2027, accelerated from its prior 2027 target. The 20 GW gross new contract additions guidance appears conservative given GEV is likely to exit the year above 125 GW in contracted gas turbines.

bullets.title: INTC foundry thesis: US government's $8.9B stake now worth $52B; 18A positioned as pragmatic partner
bullets.body: The US Government's August 2025 purchase of 433M Intel shares at $20.47 is now worth $52.2B at ~$120/share, an unrealized gain of $43.3B. Multiple analysts cited TSMC advanced node capacity as fully booked, with Intel 18A emerging as the pragmatic base die partner for memory makers including MU. Nancy Pelosi also disclosed a $3.75M+ position in INTC and Bloom Energy.

bullets.title: Consumer AI agent race heats up: Muse vs. OpenAI, Amazon blocks, QCOM/MA agentic payments
bullets.body: META's Muse was described as a high bar for consumer agents, with 1.8M downloads and 642K DAU in 12 days vs. ChatGPT's 1.3M/231K. Qualcomm and Mastercard announced a partnership for agentic payments infrastructure across Snapdragon devices. Amazon blocked Muse from its retail site, and OpenAI is reportedly developing counter-features.
